item.title: Spectral Perturbations Reveal Structured Sensitivity in LLM Capabilities
item.description:
Spectral Perturbations Reveal Structured Sensitivity in LLM Capabilities

Researchers applied spectral perturbations to the feed‑forward projections of transformer models to study how singular‑value spectra affect downstream behavior.

🔍 Overview

  • Singular‑value spectra encode important structure in transformer feed‑forward projections, but their causal role in downstream behavior has been underexplored.

🧩 How it works

  • The study performs post‑hoc spectral smoothing and spiking interventions on the up_proj and down_proj matrices.
  • Positive perturbations stretch deviations from the geometric mean, making large singular values larger and small ones smaller (spiking); negative perturbations have the opposite effect.
  • The intervention preserves the singular vectors and the geometric mean of the singular values.

⚙️ Evaluation

  • Five open‑source instruction models from the Llama and Qwen families were perturbed.
  • Evaluations covered:
    • capability‑labeled subtasks,
    • standard and chain‑of‑thought reasoning benchmarks,
    • judge‑scored truthfulness, hallucination, and safety tasks,
    • TRAIT personality probes.

📊 Findings

  • Score shifts were interpreted in a three‑dimensional capability basis: factual knowledge, language understanding, and deductive reasoning.
  • Large positive perturbations more reliably suppress language and deductive responses.
  • Moderate negative perturbations can sometimes improve factual or task‑local performance.
  • Sensitivity varies strongly by model family, benchmark module, and underlying layerwise spectral inequality.

💡 Why it matters

  • Spectral perturbation provides a lightweight intervention for probing how capabilities are organized and traded off in large language models.

#SpectralAnalysis #LLM #CapabilityProbing #Transformer

Source: Spectral Smoothing and Spiking Perturbations Reconfigure Capability Profiles and Selective Task Performance in Large Language Models

item.title: NVIDIA Releases Kumo Forecast for Multi-Variate Time-Series Forecasting
item.description:
NVIDIA Releases Kumo Forecast for Multi-Variate Time-Series Forecasting

NVIDIA has introduced Kumo Forecast (formerly known as NV-Tesseract Forecasting), a multi-variate time-series forecasting model that integrates a pretrained Transformer backbone with a context-enhanced retrieval mode.

🧩 How it works

Kumo-Forecast combines four main components to generate predictions by drawing on representations learned during pretraining and historical observations available for the current application:

Component Function
Pretrained Temporal Encoder Uses the MOMENT-1-large Transformer encoder as the backbone.
Trainable Forecasting Head Maps representations to future values for the requested horizon.
Historical-Pattern Retrieval Uses a nearest-neighbor approach to retrieve related patterns from historical data.
Interpretability Framework Produces model-agnostic explanations without modifying the forecaster.

⚙️ Key details

  • Architecture: The model uses a MOMENT-1-large backbone consisting of an approximately 340-million-parameter base encoder. During training of the forecasting head, the encoder and embedder weights remain frozen.
  • Forecasting Modes:
    • Direct Forecasting: Uses the MOMENT-based Transformer and forecasting head to predict future values, with support for autoregressive extension for horizons beyond native capability.
    • Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval (DARR): Augments direct forecasts by retrieving patterns from a separate historical DataFrame (context_df). Developers can configure the strength of reliance on each pathway.
  • Input Specifications: Supports input sequence lengths of 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 observations. Inputs must include a timestamp column and one or more numeric value columns via CSV, JSON, or pandas DataFrame.
  • Interpretability: When enabled, the framework provides an explanation bundle including trajectory-stability diagnostics, semantic-flow diagnostics, lag and feature attributions per horizon, and optional embedding Integrated Gradients.

🚀 Availability

  • License: Available under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • API: Provides a DataFrame-first API with configurable forecast horizons.
  • Integration: The Predictive Maintenance module within the Factory Operations (FOX) Blueprint leverages Kumo Forecast and Kumo Anomaly to predict future anomalies from real-time data.
  • Developer Resources: The Kumo-TS repository includes examples for fine-tuning the model on user-supplied CSVs, supporting both pretrained inference and adaptation workflows.

#NVIDIA #TimeSeries #Forecasting #MachineLearning #Transformer

Source: NVIDIA Kumo Forecast Combines Pretrained Time-Series Representations with Historical Pattern Retrieval and Interpretability

item.title: AttSVD Enables Prompt-Adaptive Low-Rank KV Cache Compression
item.description:
AttSVD Enables Prompt-Adaptive Low-Rank KV Cache Compression

AttSVD is a new, interpretable low‑rank compression method that adapts to each prompt’s attention geometry, reducing key‑value (KV) cache memory while preserving performance.

🔍 Overview

  • KV caches of autoregressive transformers grow linearly with context length and dominate memory at long context.
  • Traditional training‑free remedies evict low‑importance tokens, an irreversible choice along the sequence axis.
  • AttSVD keeps every token but stores it more cheaply along the feature axis.

🧩 How it works

  • Performs an online, per‑prompt truncated Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) that retains only the directions attention actually reads.
  • The retained rank determines the proportion of persistent per‑head KV memory that is kept.
  • Two decode‑time caching strategies are offered:
    • Accumulating – suited for short generation regimes.
    • Streaming – suited for long generation regimes.

⚙️ Key details

  • Per‑matrix energy rule: sizes the logit space and the attention mass independently.
  • Attention‑aware basis: truncates only in the spaces attention reads, preserving both attention logits and output.
  • Provides free, per‑head interpretability insights into effective rank and the geometry attention consumes.

📊 Performance

  • Across multiple models, on an agentic benchmark and the full LongBench suite, AttSVD stays on par with the dense cache while using up to 50 % of the KV‑cache memory.

#KVCache #LowRank #Transformer #MemoryEfficiency
